I can't verify what specific LLM was "released today" — I don't have real-time information about current releases, and I don't know today's date in your context. I also can't browse the web to check.

That said, I can tell you what those specifications mean:

- **Parameters: 3B** — The model has ~3 billion trainable weights. This is a "small" modern LLM, suitable for on-device or efficient inference.
- **Hidden Size: 4096** — The dimensionality of the model's internal representations (embedding/residual stream width). This is relatively large for a 3B model (many 3B models use 2560 or 3072).
- **Layers: 16** — The number of transformer blocks stacked. This is shallow compared to typical 3B models (which often have 26–32 layers). The model is "wide and shallow."
- **Heads: 32** — Number of attention heads per layer (each head would be 4096/32 = 128 dimensions, a common head size).
- **Sequence Length: 4096** — The context window — the model can attend to 4096 tokens at once. This is modest by 2024–2025 standards (many newer models support 32K–1M+).

The **wide-and-shallow** shape (4096 hidden / 16 layers) is unusual and notable — it suggests the designers optimized for inference speed (fewer sequential layer computations) or for specific hardware. Models like some MobileLLM variants or speculative-decoding draft models use similar shapes.

If you can share the model's name or a link, I can give you a more specific answer.
